contributions.summary: Game-theory combined AHP-EWM weighting with TOPSIS for multi-criteria client selection.
SIRS-inspired OPN compartmental model for wildlife product demand dynamics.
Modified Lotka-Volterra SPW model linking poaching to enforcement resources.
FIWT difference equation model with logistic government strike factor.
FWP population model with linearly increasing growth rate from ecosystem effort.

assumptions.summary: Data from global organization databases is precise and trustworthy.
Illegal wildlife trade is driven by market demand.
Wildlife growth rate will not change significantly in 5 years without intervention.

data_and_preprocessing.summary: Client indicator data from 8 organization official websites with missing value filling.
LPI estimates from WWF and ZSL for 1975-2023.
UNODC World WISE seizure database: ivory and rhino horn = 70% of seizures.
Population data from major participating countries summed to S.

models.summary: CA model: AHP-EWM-TOPSIS for client ranking (WWF score 0.78).
OPN model: SIRS-based ODE for buyer transitions (41.2% purchaser decrease in 5 years).
SPW model: Modified Lotka-Volterra for poaching dynamics (46.64% poaching decrease).
FIWT model: Difference equation for monthly trade volume (52.4% reduction).
FWP model: Population projection with ecosystem improvement (9.3% population increase).

verification.summary: AHP consistency ratio CR=0.068<0.1 passes consistency check.
Sensitivity analysis: coefficient perturbation on OPN and SPW shows stable trends.
Uncertainty analysis with high negative impact scenario: 49.6% trade decrease, 6.9% population increase.

results_trace.summary: WWF selected as ideal client with TOPSIS score 0.78.
Purchaser population reduced by 41.2% through publicity strategies.
Poaching decreased by 46.64% through enforcement investment.
Illegal trade volume reduced by 52.4% over 5 years.
Wildlife population increased by 9.3% (6.1% even under uncertainty).
S = 3,654,189,667 total population across analyzed countries
Budget estimate ~$6.51 million for poaching protection

judge_relevance_hypotheses.summary: Clear task-indexed structure with quantitative outcomes signals organized approach.
SIRS epidemiological analogy for demand modeling shows creative cross-domain application.
Lotka-Volterra adaptation for enforcement-poaching dynamics demonstrates modeling creativity.
Professional memo format with quantitative backing meets F-type communication requirement.

weaknesses.summary: Data limitations: not all indicator data available, some initial values estimated from government reports.
Used data from selected countries only (India, China, Myanmar) - not globally representative.
OPN model assumes homogeneous mixing in population of 3.6 billion.
FWP linear growth rate increase ignores carrying capacity and density dependence.
FIWT model has no stochastic component for enforcement variability.

independent_extensions.summary: Add spatial heterogeneity or network structure to OPN compartmental model.
Add logistic carrying capacity to FWP population model.
Add stochastic perturbation to FIWT trade forecasting.
